answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. What this achieves is a system where the cost of an attack is public and provable, so the whole network can trust verdicts without trusting any single identity.. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. Consider a sonnet as the anchor of the cost.
